[01:14:26] is if you learn the gain term in RMS norm,
[01:14:31] this turns out to break muP.
[01:14:33] Although, these can be removed in many cases
[01:14:35] without necessarily hurting you, and so maybe
[01:14:38] it's not such a bad idea.
[01:14:39] But this does seem to break muP.
[01:14:42] It also seems to break if you use more exotic optimizers
[01:14:44] like Lion, which basically rely on the sign of the gradient.
[01:14:48] And sign gradient is like a spiritually
[01:14:51] similar to muon and other ideas.
[01:14:53] And so there might be other interesting things
[01:14:54] that break with muP as well.
[01:14:58] Finally, the thing that seems most concerning
[01:15:01] is that if you do large decoupled weight decay,
[01:15:04] you end up with significant muP failure.
[01:15:07] So this is maybe the one stress test that it does fail.
[01:15:11] But to close out this final section, you might, in the end,
[01:15:14] ask, like, is muP useful?
[01:15:16] And if you really want to stabilize your learning rates,
[01:15:19] it is actually pretty useful.
[01:15:21] There's a lot of experiments of this form, where
[01:15:24] if you increase the width, your optimal learning rate shifts
[01:15:26] very predictably, but very greatly as a function of scale.
[01:15:30] Whereas, with muP it doesn't.
[01:15:31] And so it's one of the many tools in the toolkit
[01:15:34] to try to control hyperparameter drift as a function of scale.
[01:15:38] I think it's an interesting open area of research.
[01:15:40] It's not really done and dusted, and this
[01:15:43] is the one right thing to do.
[01:15:44] But there's a lot of promise in the muP-style initialization
[01:15:47] program.
[01:15:47] There's also a lot of promise in just fitting scaling laws
[01:15:50] as well.
[01:15:52] So final thing I want to close with, scaling in the wild
[01:15:57] is very tricky.
[01:15:58] As I mentioned in one of my replies.
[01:16:00] I think the initial presentation of scaling laws
[01:16:03] makes it sound like a science.
[01:16:05] It's like, yes, draw this line, do these procedures,
[01:16:07] and you will know, for sure, what will happen at scale.
[01:16:11] But I think, in reality, it's a lot more messy and a lot more
[01:16:14] unknown than that.
[01:16:16] There are lots of things that people
[01:16:18] do use in practice scaling laws for,
[01:16:20] like picking architectures, picking optimizers, picking
[01:16:22] hyperparameters.
[01:16:23] All of these things are things that people
[01:16:25] do with scaling laws, but there is really an art to it
[01:16:28] in the sense of, you don't really
[01:16:29] if it's truly going to extrapolate forever.
[01:16:32] You want to do reasonable things to maximize
[01:16:35] the chances of success.
[01:16:36] And so there's lots of solutions that people have.
[01:16:38] You can use muP.
[01:16:39] You can search for the optimal learning rate in all
[01:16:42] of these other kinds of things.
[01:16:43] And these are ways of controlling hyperparameter
[01:16:46] drift.
[01:16:47] But there's no silver bullet yet.
[01:16:48] Maybe next year, there will be a module
[01:16:50] that's like, we solved it, but not quite yet.
[01:16:53] Great Thanks a lot.
[01:16:55] I can take questions afterwards.
